# Model overview

**MOOOD** is an open-source discrete-event simulation developed by Richard Pilbery and colleagues. It follows callers after an NHS 111 primary-care disposition and represents subsequent contact with primary care, NHS 111, ambulance services and emergency departments. The Python and SimPy model compares the existing system with timely primary-care contact and reports activity across services and avoidable ED attendance.

The original data and parameters relate to callers registered with Bradford and Airedale GP practices, so reuse elsewhere requires local review and validation.

## Actions for participants before the session

- Retain the working environment and editable repository from Session 1 (if you did not attend Session 1, confirm that you can complete a model run before this session).
- Consider one assumption or feature you would change.
- Make the change to the code.
- Consider how you would test whether the change you have made has been successful.
- If time permits, test the functionality of the code.

::: {.callout-warning title="Local software requirement"}
**This model uses Python.** To run it locally, you will need Python installed and will need to set up the packages and environment described in the repository.
:::

## Getting help

If you have a problem running or reusing MOOOD, the model's issue tracker will be the best way to contact the ReModel team. **Issue tracker link: [to be added].** When reporting a problem, describe what you were trying to do, what happened and any error messages you received.

## Session objectives and outline

This will be a discussion session around our attempts to edit and reuse the model. Participants will discuss:

- what changes they made to the repository and how they went about doing it;
- how they went about testing the change, or how they would plan to test the change they made;
- how changes should be documented and integrated with existing documentation;
- whether any changes to the repository would have made running or reusing the model easier.

The aim is for participants to leave the session with a clear understanding of how to make changes to a repository and how to test that those changes work as intended.

## Additional resources

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/MOOOD-study) — source code, tests and configuration.
- [HSMA project page](https://hsma.co.uk/previous_projects/hsma_4/h4_4008_meeting_demand_111/index.html) — project background and supporting material.
- [Healthcare Service Analytics & Decision Intelligence Atlas review](https://atlas.hsma.co.uk/packages_projects_tools/meeting_the_demand_of_111/) — assessment of documentation, testing, reproducibility and deployment.
- [University of Plymouth research record](https://researchportal.plymouth.ac.uk/en/publications/modelling-nhs-england-111-demand-for-primary-care-services-a-disc/) — publication details and related outputs.
- [Supporting observational study](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0300193) — analysis of NHS 111 demand for primary-care services.

Reuse elsewhere will require local review and validation of the demand, capacity, pathway and behavioural assumptions.
